## Exercise Overview

In this coding colab, you'll analyze global temperature anomalies and CO2 concentration data. You'll practice data manipulation, joining datasets, time series analysis, and visualization techniques.

## Setup

Let's start by importing necessary libraries and loading our datasets:

```{python}
#| echo: true

import pandas as pd

# Load the temperature anomaly dataset
temp_url = "https://eds-217-essential-python.github.io/data/monthly_temperature_data.csv"
temp_df = pd.read_csv(temp_url, parse_dates=['Date'])

# Load the CO2 concentration dataset
co2_url = "https://eds-217-essential-python.github.io/data/monthly_co2_concentration.csv"
co2_df = pd.read_csv(co2_url, parse_dates=['Date'])

print("Temperature data:")
print(temp_df.head())
print("\nCO2 data:")
print(co2_df.head())
```

## Task 1: Data Preparation

### 1. Set the 'Date' column as the index for both dataframes

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

temp_df.set_index('Date', inplace=True)
co2_df.set_index('Date', inplace=True)

print("Set Date as index for both dataframes")
```

### 2. Check for missing values

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

print("Missing values in temperature data:", temp_df.isnull().sum().sum())
print("Missing values in CO2 data:", co2_df.isnull().sum().sum())
```

## Task 2: Joining Datasets

### 1. Merge the temperature and CO2 datasets

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

combined_df = pd.merge(temp_df, co2_df, left_index=True, right_index=True, how='inner')
print("Merged datasets")
```

### 2. Handle missing values from the merge

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

combined_df.fillna(method='ffill', inplace=True)
print("Filled missing values")
```

### 3. Create plots showing temperature anomalies and CO2 concentrations

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

# Temperature anomaly plot
combined_df['MonthlyAnomaly'].plot(
    figsize=(12, 4), color='red', 
    title='Monthly Global Temperature Anomalies',
    ylabel='Temperature Anomaly (°C)')

# CO2 concentration plot  
combined_df['CO2Concentration'].plot(
    figsize=(12, 4), color='blue',
    title='Monthly CO2 Concentration',
    ylabel='CO2 Concentration (ppm)')
```

## Task 3: Time Series Analysis

### 1. Resample data to annual averages

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

annual_data = combined_df.resample('YE').mean()
print(annual_data.head())
```

### 2. Calculate year-over-year changes

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

annual_data['Temp_YoY_Change'] = annual_data['MonthlyAnomaly'].diff()
annual_data['CO2_YoY_Change'] = annual_data['CO2Concentration'].diff()

print(annual_data[['Temp_YoY_Change', 'CO2_YoY_Change']].head(10))
```

### 3. Create scatter plot of temperature vs CO2

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

annual_data.plot(
    kind='scatter', 
    x='CO2Concentration', 
    y='MonthlyAnomaly', 
    figsize=(10, 6), 
    title='Annual Temperature Anomaly vs CO2 Concentration'
)
```

## Task 4: Seasonal Analysis

### 1. Create function to extract season

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

def get_season(date):
    month = date.month
    if month in [12, 1, 2]:
        return 'Winter'
    elif month in [3, 4, 5]:
        return 'Spring'
    elif month in [6, 7, 8]:
        return 'Summer'
    else:
        return 'Fall'
```

### 2. Add Season column to dataframe

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

combined_df['Season'] = pd.Series(combined_df.index, index=combined_df.index).apply(get_season)

# combined_df['Season'] = combined_df.index.map(get_season)

print("Added Season column")
print(combined_df.head())
```

### 3. Calculate seasonal averages

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

seasonal_avg = combined_df.groupby('Season').mean()
print("Seasonal Averages:")
print(seasonal_avg)
```

### 4. Create box plot of temperature anomalies by season

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| include: true

combined_df.boxplot(
    column='MonthlyAnomaly',
    by='Season', 
    figsize=(10, 6)
)
```
